diagnostic_rule: DIAGNOSTIC_PENETRATION_NOT_ADOPTABLE: the edge enters the rigid board; never a candidate

blade_vs_fixture_code_answer.summary: TLMPM does not know that the board is rigid for the blade. The kinematic blade is a prescribed SDF that acts only on material particles. Nothing stops, resists or reports a blade entering a fixture box. Fixture boxes act only on material particles, through a per-particle penalty impulse with Coulomb friction. There is no grid boundary condition.
details: kinematic_env.py:135-136 (HEAD dd1538b): the edge is set to the commanded target with no collision check and passed to LiveCuttingMaterial.advance. live_material.py:265 assigns the interpolated poses to the solver unchanged.

tlmpm_v5.py:185-296 _rigid_contacts: the blade is the convex polygon SDF (_profile_sdf, :231) minus the contact radius 0.45 mm. Its impulse ji goes into the particle impulse (:290) and its negative into the tool reaction (:292). Only material particles are tested. No fixture box is ever compared with the blade pose. stats[3] (:296) is the max blade-into-material penetration, not blade-into-board.
tlmpm_v5.py:299-327 _obstacle_contacts: the handle box is tool-attached and also pushes material only.

tlmpm_v5.py:720-733 and 848-851: the fixture boxes and table plane (live_material.py:178-180, built from task.fixture_boxes_local with floor=False and fixture_walls=False at :167) go only to the fixture_contacts kernel. fixture_contacts.py:11-28 runs per particle: the box SDF gap is sdf - radius, the impulse is _contact_impulse (tlmpm.py:113-123: penalty jn = k m/dt max(-predicted gap, 0) with k = contact_stiffness 0.1, and friction capped at mu jn with mu = contact_friction = material friction 0.3), and stats[0] is the max fixture/table penetration. The impulse enters P2G with gravity (tlmpm_v5.py:513). _grid_update (tlmpm_v5.py:532) applies no boundary condition.

The board impulse is not in bed.reaction (live_material.py:282 reads blade and handle only), so no runtime output reports board forces. This study measures them by material momentum balance (dP - M g dt + reaction) and cross-checks with a NumPy replica of the fixture kernel. At rest this gives 1.413 N against a weight of 1.413 N.

Planning is the only place that knows about supports. goal_planner._relief_end (goal_planner.py:237-250) ends a through-cut on the support top when the edge line below the bar would hit a support. That is why the compiled sever_mid plan on the solid board stops at local z = 0.

Grid domain: tlmpm_v5.py:734-735 builds the grid origin and dims from particle positions only. The board's x/y size does not change the domain or the node count (5850 nodes, dims [45, 13, 10] in every row). Fixture cost is O(particles x boxes) per substep (fixture_contacts.py:19), which is negligible.

analysis_notes.bottom_layer_observation: On the solid board and the 8 mm slot, the bottom-layer particles near the cut lift from their resting centre height of 0.43 mm to 0.80-0.92 mm by the end of the cut. The wedge spreads the halves and the soft provisional material (E 50 kPa, yield 1 kPa) curls up at the cut faces. 308 layer-0 particles end above 0.6 mm; far from the cut the bottom stays at 0.431 mm. The law-4 band (used by law 8; the law-8 lead rule is inactive for a vertical non-plowing descent) labels particles by their current position relative to the edge (local x <= 0). So the clean-cut margin above the board comes partly from this lift and the 0.45 mm resting height. It depends on the material and is not a robust tolerance. At h = +1.0 mm, 172 of 240 layer-0 particles in the |x| < 4 mm stencil column stay unassigned. At +0.5 mm, 16 stay unassigned. At +0.375 mm and below, none do. Only layer 0 is ever bridged.

recommendation.primary: Option A, made explicit as A+B. Cut to the board surface: end the armed descent with the edge's lowest point exactly at the board top (h = 0, which is what goal_planner._relief_end already plans for a solid board). On cutting_tasks_v1 at 1 mm, h = 0, +0.25 and +0.375 mm all give a clean, persistent two-piece through-cut with zero code-0 bridges and all 30 layer-0 cross-plane links conflicting. h = +0.5 mm leaves 16 bridging particles and one component; h = +1.0 mm leaves 172.
recommendation.option_B: Physical contact. In TLMPM the board is real only for the material: zero particle centres inside the board in every row, max penalty-shell penetration 72-101 um on solid and 8 mm boards, fixture Fz mean during the cut 1.421 N against a weight of 1.413 N. TLMPM has no blade-board contact, so no blade force is blocked. In Native, PhysX knife-board contact must stop the edge at the board top and must be monitored: an edge below the top is a violation, never a silent pass-through. If PhysX stops the edge above h = +0.375 mm, the bottom layer stays bridged; report that as the Option-B limitation.
recommendation.option_C: A sacrificial or compliant board needs a new deformable board model (e.g. a second TLMPM body or a compliant contact law). That is a physics change, out of scope here; kept as a documented study item only. S_M025_DIAG shows that 0.25 mm of penetration buys nothing over h = 0 (identical topology), so there is no cutting reason to need it.
recommendation.option_D: An explicit slotted board stays an opt-in scene option for cuts that must pass below the workpiece bottom (oblique or tilted planes, overtravel plans). The 8 mm slot cuts cleanly at h = -4 mm and h = 0. A 40 mm gap (CUT-01-R) needs the overtravel: at h = 0 the unsupported bar sags 0.5-0.9 mm into the gap and 48 bridging particles remain (FAIL), while h = -4 mm passes (M1a-equivalent). Never a hidden default.
recommendation.never: S_M025_DIAG (h = -0.25 mm) puts the edge 0.25 mm inside the rigid board. TLMPM neither detects nor resists it (stats have no blade-fixture term), so it is DIAGNOSTIC_PENETRATION_NOT_ADOPTABLE and never a candidate.
recommendation.caveats: Kinematic ideal tracking with a single seed and a single material (provisional, uncalibrated) at 1 mm spacing and 4 mm grid. The margin above the board depends on the resting height (contact radius) and the bottom-layer lift, so it must be re-measured for other materials, spacings and live tracking error.
